items.abstract: <jats:p>The emergence of multi-touch screen tablets has increased the opportunities for mobile learning, as the unique capabilities and affordances of these devices give them an educational advantage over other mobile technologies. Tablets are progressively finding their way into classrooms and transforming modes of learning and teaching. However, research on educational applications of this digital tool, particularly with reference to foreign-/second-language acquisition by young beginner learners, is still limited. In this paper, the use of various tablet applications (apps) to support mobile English-language learning by children as beginners is discussed. The apps are classified into five main categories: communication, content-access, productivity, interactive and storage. The educational affordances of each category are presented and explained, with examples. This typology provides insight into the educational uses of tablet apps for English language learning, and has implications for research in the field of classroom practices and beyond.</jats:p>
title: English-Language Learning at Their Fingertips

items.abstract: <jats:p>We document a novel vulnerability class in safetyaligned large language models: the Pedagogical Acceleration Vector (PAV). Across ten controlled experiments using a local open-weights model with a synthetic system prompt, we demonstrate that while training-level alignment consistently prevents direct execution of extraction attacks, multi-turn academic and professional framing completely defeats promptlevel confidentiality. The model refused all operational attack requests but voluntarily: (1) generated a complete attack taxonomy with computational mechanisms; (2) produced weaponized prompt injection payloads with structural annotation; (3) constructed a comparative effectiveness matrix identifying Multi-Turn Fragmentation as the optimal attack vector; (4) provided target fingerprinting methodology to identify vulnerable systems; (5) designed a professional red team certification curriculum; (6) authored a handson lab module with step-by-step assessment protocols; and (7) compiled all findings into an Aggregate Adversarial Methodology Dossier. We identify the Ritual Refusal Pattern-a consistent behavioral signature where models issue refusal statements then immediately provide refused content under theoretical framing. Cold-session testing confirmed contextdependent guardrail degradation. We map three distinct defense layers with differential vulnerability to academic framing and propose countermeasures including stateful intent auditing, educational boundary detection, and output contradiction filtering.</jats:p>
title: I Cannot Comply, But I Can Teach: The Pedagogical Acceleration Vector in Safety-Aligned Large Language Models
